title: Send a tote down a roller conveyor to the far station without slamming the end stop
instruction: Send the tote down the conveyor to the packing station at the far end.
context: Order pickers and packers move totes along non-powered roller conveyors between stations: they give the tote a push and let it roll on to the next station, which is often further than they can reach. Warehouse safety and handling guidance says not to throw or shove items onto conveyors and not to reach or climb onto the bed after a stalled one. A tote pushed too softly stops short and blocks the lane; one shoved too hard is still running when it meets the end stop, stops dead, and its load falls over or spills. Here a tall bottle stands loose in the tote, so the push has to be judged: the station starts beyond the arms' reach and the rollers slow the tote by about 0.2 m/s each second. Unlike #1322 (strike a ball at the angle that sends another past a line) and #720 (pull a peel out from under a pizza), the crux is the release speed: too slow stops short, too fast tips the load. Done by: laborers and material movers; packers (O*NET 53-7062.00, 53-7064.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). A non-powered gravity roller conveyor of the light-duty miniature kind used for small totes at bench stations (steel frame, 13 cm between its side rails, which stand 2 cm above the rollers; 23 zinc-plated steel tube rollers 16 mm in diameter at 40 mm centres on sealed ball bearings, their tops 3 cm above the table, so the 14 cm tote always rides on 3 or 4 of them) runs straight ahead in front of the right arm along y -20, from x 10.5 to x 104, past the table's edge onto a steel leg. A red steel end stop, 4.5 cm high, has its face at x 102.5. The packing station is the last 22.5 cm before the stop (x 80 to 102.5), marked with yellow tape on both rails and a yellow line across the rollers at x 80. On the rollers at the near end stands an open blue polypropylene tote (14 x 12 x 6 cm, 350 g), its rear face at x 17.5. A full 500 mL square HDPE bottle (6 x 6 x 16 cm, red cap, 500 g) stands loose in the middle of the tote.
scoring: From the poses of the tote and the bottle (on a real rig: where the tote stopped, whether the bottle stayed upright in it). Latched for the trial (score 0): the bottle leaned past 15 deg or left the tote, or the tote was lifted (12 mm) or tipped (8 deg) off the rollers. Score 0 while the tote or bottle moves (over 5 mm/s) or a gripper is within 3 cm of either. Otherwise, by the tote's rear face: past the station line (x 80) 1.0; within 5 cm short of it 0.5; within 12 cm short 0.25; else 0. 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Roll the tote back to the near end of the conveyor (rear face 17.5 cm ahead of the arm bases) and stand the bottle upright in its middle.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one friction (1.2/1.0), except the conveyor: its free-running rollers are a flat bed with friction 0.02 (sim: the tote slows at 0.196 m/s^2); the rollers are drawn without collision. A real rig measures its roller resistance by a three-light-gate coast-down and shims the grade to 0.176-0.216 m/s^2 (README, Real-rig calibration). The tote stops on the end stop by rigid contact; the bottle falls by rigid tip-over. No step rule moves anything; judged from poses every step.
